promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 8 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: Do not make up the missed miles. The cuts came from heat, short sleep and stress, so run about 28 miles next week, keep one smaller threshold session and rebuild the long run from 10 miles.

flags.title: Cut sessions

answers.question: I missed Thursday and cut the long run short. Should I make up the miles next week?
answers.answer:
No, leave the missed miles behind. About 9 of the 36 planned miles did not happen, and heat, short sleep and the work deadline caused that, not a lack of fitness.

Adding them back would stack extra load on a body already running 13 beats per minute higher at a slower pace. That is how you end up with a flat week or a setback like the knee gave you in mid-August.

Next week is about 28 miles, one mile above what you actually ran. The long run goes back to 10 miles, and it matters far more than the Thursday run you missed.

new.analysis:
## What happened

| Day | Planned | What you ran |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tue Aug 25 | Easy, 6 mi | 6.0 mi at 10:24/mi, heart rate 153 |
| Wed Aug 26 | 8 mi with 3 x 1.5 mi at 8:00/mi | 6.0 mi, 2 reps at 8:18/mi, then stopped |
| Thu Aug 27 | Easy, 5 mi | Missed |
| Sat Aug 29 | Easy, 4 mi | 4.0 mi at 10:34/mi, heart rate 149 |
| Sun Aug 30 | Long, 13 mi, heart rate under 150 | 11.0 mi at 11:14/mi, heart rate 156, two water stops |

The week came to 27 of 36 planned miles. Heat, sleep and stress explain nearly all of the gap.

Stopping on Wednesday and Sunday was the right call. The Wednesday reps were slower than planned at effort 9/10, and you rated how you felt 3/10. Pushing on would have cost recovery without adding fitness.

Your easy runs show what the heat cost you. Their heart rate put them in zone 3, so easy running fell to 11% of the week against 65 to 77% in earlier weeks. Your easy pace and heart rate were steady for three weeks before this, so I read it as short-term strain, not lost fitness.

The plan also asked for 36 miles straight after a 24-mile week. That was a steep step even before the heat and the broken air conditioning, so I am not pushing the build through it.

This week is a reset, not a step up. Threshold stays in at about half the size, because a full session on short sleep in heat digs a hole you then have to climb out of. The long run stays at 10 miles, a distance you handled at heart rate 146 on Aug 23, so you rebuild rhythm without more heat stress.

With 8 weeks to go, one flat week costs little and does not change the goal. Once the air conditioning is fixed and sleep returns, the long run can climb again and a medium-long run during the week comes back.

Treat sleep as training this week. A cool shower before bed, a fan and a short daytime nap all help. Run at the coolest hour you can get, and plan water stops on a loop route.

settingsProposalBullets: In cool weather your easy runs sit at 138 to 140 bpm, so cap easy days at 148 bpm in heat instead of chasing pace.
Your apartment air conditioning is broken until about next week and work stress is high, so sleep gets planned as part of training.
Your right knee had an outside-of-knee flare in mid-August that settled, so keep hip and glute work in the routine.

safetyCallouts.title: Take the fatigue and heat seriously.
safetyCallouts.body: Stop, get into the shade and cool down if you feel dizzy, nauseous or chilled on a run, and get medical help if it does not pass. If the tiredness stays after your sleep and the heat ease, talk to a doctor.
